## Structure and components

- [statement] Atlas Agent Engine offers a modular agent platform: customers can adopt a layer or the full stack. Independent analysis also describes component adoption as separable from a database architecture migration. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/index.md · keywords: Atlas Agent Engine architecture and components · also: https://theweightedaverage.com/posts/2026-09-30-atlas-infinite-agent-migration-gates/
- [statement] Independent analysis recommends evaluating Agent Engine components independently and requiring an explicit compatibility map before coupling adoption to Atlas Infinite. Its architecture distinction is that a unified product announcement does not establish compatibility between every agent component and a newly announced database architecture. (low confidence) — https://theweightedaverage.com/posts/2026-09-30-atlas-infinite-agent-migration-gates/ · keywords: Atlas Agent Engine architecture and components

## How it works

- [statement] The execution architecture separates agent graph execution from remote tool execution: local tools run in the agent process, while remote tool bodies run on demand in the Tool Sandbox or Tool Pod when OE routes them. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/reference/agent-contract.md · keywords: Atlas Agent Engine architecture and components · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/sdk/python/packages/agent-engine-runner-shared.md

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] The shared runner is an internal dependency of framework SDKs rather than the package agent authors normally install; Python documentation names LangGraph and ADK adapters, while the TypeScript shared runner names its LangGraph adapter. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/sdk/python/packages/agent-engine-runner-shared.md · keywords: Atlas Agent Engine architecture and components · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/sdk/javascript/packages/agent-engine-runner-shared.md
- [statement] Agent authors expose an in-process `App` object rather than implementing an HTTP endpoint. The Python contract uses `agent.yaml` to resolve a module attribute, registers graph construction with `@app.entrypoint`, and starts the application with `app.run()`. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/reference/agent-contract.md · keywords: Atlas Agent Engine architecture and components
- [statement] Checkpoint state is separate from a live sandbox process: agent sandboxes are ephemeral, and MongoDB stores graph checkpoints between suspend and resume. Graph state must be JSON/BSON-serializable rather than containing live connections, file handles or unsupported custom objects. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/reference/agent-contract.md · keywords: Atlas Agent Engine architecture and components

## Facts and statements

- [statement] The Runner SDK integrates the Agent Execution Runtime (AER), Tool Pod, and Memory Server; the Orchestration Engine (OE) is a separate service, with AER running agent logic and Tool Pod providing isolated tool execution. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/sdk/python/packages/agent-engine-runner-shared.md · keywords: Atlas Agent Engine architecture and components
- [statement] The TypeScript runner-shared package supplies protocol handling, secure call wrappers, request-scoped context and server adapters; it is an open-source integration library, and does not distribute the managed OE or AER services. Agent authors install a framework SDK that depends on it. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/sdk/javascript/packages/agent-engine-runner-shared.md · keywords: Atlas Agent Engine architecture and components
- [statement] Intercepted calls cross OE before execution. OE owns routing and returns the final outcome; remote tool calls use Tool Pod execution, while approved local calls return to the original AER call stack. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/sdk/python/packages/agent-engine-runner-shared.md · keywords: Atlas Agent Engine architecture and components · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/reference/agent-contract.md
- [statement] The wrapper boundary limits the architecture’s guarantees: the Agent Contract states that calls outside `app.tool(...)` and `app.llm(...)` are not audited and do not replay correctly after resume. Universal governance or replay must not be inferred for arbitrary unwrapped application code. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/reference/agent-contract.md · keywords: Atlas Agent Engine architecture and components
- [statement] The MongoDB agent templates illustrate the runtime split by running model and MCP calls in a tool sandbox separate from the agent. (low confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/agents · keywords: Atlas Agent Engine architecture and components
- [statement] The official pages give conflicting entrypoint-construction timings: Runner SDK architecture says tool application construction attempts the entrypoint during startup; Agent Contract says startup does not run the entrypoint and the Tool Sandbox loads it lazily on the first LLM invocation. These are attributed documentation positions, not a resolved statement of runtime behavior. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/sdk/python/packages/agent-engine-runner-shared.md · keywords: Atlas Agent Engine architecture and components · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/reference/agent-contract.md
- [statement] Resume combines graph checkpointing with OE-owned replay caching for wrapped operations. OE returns previously stored outcomes for replayed calls to avoid repeating their side effects; a cached response is distinct from executing a new call. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/sdk/python/packages/agent-engine-runner-shared.md · keywords: Atlas Agent Engine architecture and components · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/reference/agent-contract.md
